topSignals.title: Topsoe's only data-center-adjacent news this week turns out to be a different technology path entirely — not SOFC/SOEC.
topSignals.text: Topsoe announced on Oct 29 that it is technology licensor for HDF Energy's "BaseBlue Power" project in Texas: a 250 MW low-carbon power plant for data centers, using Topsoe's SynCOR autothermal-reforming (ATR) process to make ~400 t/day of blue hydrogen (>95% CO2 capture, ~1.1 Mt/yr) that is then burned in HDF's own PEM fuel cells — no solid-oxide technology involved, and no Topsoe SOEC/SOFC content at all. Power is targeted for 2030. For Dominic: this confirms Topsoe is pursuing the AI-data-center power opportunity through its legacy ATR/hydrogen-licensing business, not through SOEC — a data point for how little competitive pressure Topsoe is currently putting on the SOFC side of this market, even as it chases the same customer base via a different route. Topsoe press release

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news-archive item since Sept 21 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed by direct fetch today — 40 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed by direct fetch today — 65 days quiet. Topsoe's Oct 29 press release (see Top Signals) is data-center-relevant but is an ATR/blue-hydrogen licensing deal, not an SOEC/SOFC item, and does not end the quiet streak.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation — round 2 (Sunfire, SolydEra): no new stack/cell-technology items for either. Sunfire results repeated the standing Schwarzheide SOEC test-facility construction story (BASF site, commissioning targeted end of 2026); SolydEra results repeated the standing Hannover Messe PMX-platform launch and the Dynelectro 1 MW electrolyser partnership, both already logged.

Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": no new item; results recycled standing Bloom/Ceres/FuelCell Energy earnings and data-center-deal background already in the archive.

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation — cycle 5, round 4, completing this cycle's roster (Denso, Thermax): no new items for either. Denso results were 2025-vintage SOEC/green-hydrogen strategy background (Nishio plant demonstration); Thermax results repeated the standing Ceres-Thermax SOEC partnership and a Jan 30, 2026 HPCL clean-energy MoU that is not SOFC/SOEC-specific.

Tier 3 sweeps — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR Doosan Fuel Cell OR SK ecoplant" and "Watt Fuel Cell OR OxEon Energy OR Nexceris OR Kawasaki Heavy Industries OR Miura OR Weichai": no new item for either sweep; results repeated the standing Sept 18 Doosan-Reverion $78M stack order/250 MW factory raise, Convion's 2024 HD Hyundai acquisition history, SK ecoplant's 2023-vintage GDS Singapore story, and Ceres-Miura's 4.2kW Japan product launch.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway, hearing Dec 7), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B, Vineland NJ — first power block reported ready Oct 22; block capacity undisclosed; site not yet operational), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
